query: Starting from an as-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state and a target density below 6 g/cm3, what single intervention could overcome performance limitations associated with stable intermetallic formation while improving room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts measurable changes relative to the as-processed baseline, defines the relevant composition, temperature, exposure-time, and test-environment boundaries, cites supporting evidence from previously reported Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys, and proposes a controlled experiment whose outcome could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introduction of a specific alloying element can overcome performance limitations in Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys.
generation.intervention: Addition of a small amount of alloying element, such as Sc or Y
generation.conditions: Target density below 6 g/cm3, room temperature, and high-temperature oxidation environment
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a stable, refined grain structure and precipitation of nanoscale intermetallics
generation.mechanism: Grain refinement and precipitation of nanoscale intermetallics, leading to improved compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation, relative to the as-processed baseline
generation.boundary: Composition: 0-5 at.% alloying element; Temperature: 20-500°C; Exposure time: 1-100 hours; Test environment: Air, saltwater, or acidic solution
generation.uncertainty: Insufficient evidence to determine the optimal alloying element and composition

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled experiment with varying alloying element compositions and test conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the introduction of the alloying element does not result in improved compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation, relative to the as-processed baseline, then the hypothesis is falsified.
